newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures end down, funds heavy sellers.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures end down, funds heavy sellers.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled weaker but off the lows amid technically-driven fund liquidation, floor sources said.

The selling came on the heel's of Monday's weak close and was exacerbated by today's NYCE weekly spec/hedge report. The report showed the speculators to be holding a hefty 18.3 percent net long position as of March 14.
Buying from domestic mills lifted prices off the lows on the close, dealers said. They added that weakness in CBOT corn did not contribute to losses in cotton.
Most-active May fell below its downside target of 74.00 cents to the low of 73.80 cents. The contract settled at 74.20, 0.71 cent lower.
The back months ended down 0.62 to 0.10, with new-crop December easing 0.37 on the day to close at 76.43 cents.
Volume was brisk at an estimated 25,000 lots, compared to Monday's official 5,990 lots.
Market analysts said severe flooding in the Southeast, which has sparked fears that cotton area could be lost, has contributed to the relative strength in the deferred contracts.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration underscored those fears today when it said additional flooding was likely in the Mississippi and in parts of the Southeast.

Players await the U.S. Department of Agriculture's first estimate of planted area for the 1997/98 crop, on March 31. The cotton crop is planted around the second week in April, throughout much of the Southeast.
